nodes_add.name: Arumuga Navalar
nodes_add.note: Jaffna Shaiva scholar and publisher; rejected Ramalingam's Tiruvarutpa as Marutpa (the Arutpa-Marutpa dispute, 1867 to 1904 by Tamil Wiki's dating)

nodes_add.name: Thozhuvur Velayutha Mudaliar
nodes_add.note: Ramalingam's principal disciple; edited and published the first volume of the Tiruvarutpa (Madras, 1867) with a biography

nodes_add.name: Savitribai Phule
nodes_add.note: Married Jotirao 1840; taught by him from 1841; first woman teacher at the Poona girls' school of 1848; headed the Satyashodhak Samaj women's section

nodes_update.note: Born Bellur 14 Dec 1918; sickly childhood; lived with Krishnamacharya in Mysore from about 1934; Pune from 1937; Light on Yoga 1966; props and timed, sequenced alignment; RIMYI Pune 1975; died Pune 20 Aug 2014.

Born Gagode 11 Sept 1895; met Gandhi 7 June 1916; Gitai and Talks on the Gita (Dhulia jail 1932); Bhoodan from 18 April 1951 (Pochampally); gramdan from May 1952; Brahma Vidya Mandir 1959; died Paunar 15 Nov 1982.

edges_upsert.note: Student from the 1927 Hassan demonstration; again at Mysore from about 1932; taught at the palace yogashala; left in charge of the Mysore teaching when Krishnamacharya moved to Chennai (by 1956). Yoga Korunta descent rests on Krishnamacharya's account.
Brother-in-law; Iyengar lived in his Mysore household from about 1934; relationship described as difficult.
Sannyasa 12 Sept 1947; in 1956 sent him out to teach and, by the Bihar School's account, gave him kriya yoga.
By his own account, as reported by Wikipedia and the Bihar School, he met her as a young man and she blessed him.
Principal disciple and editor of the 1867 Tiruvarutpa.
Navalar attacked the Tiruvarutpa as Marutpa; dispute dated 1867 to 1904 by Tamil Wiki.
Married 1840; he taught her to read and write from 1841; she taught in the 1848 girls' school.

glossary.def: A Vedic austerity in which the practitioner sits outdoors among four fires beneath the sun; Satyananda practised it at Rikhia.
A renunciant of the highest rank; Satyananda lived at Rikhia as a paramahamsa after 1989.
A Marathi folk theatre of song and comic scenes; the Satyashodhak Samaj used it to carry its message to peasants.
The way Ashtanga yoga is taught in Pattabhi Jois's tradition: each student practises a memorised series alone at their own pace in a shared room while the teacher helps individually.

issues: periyar.mdx: ThePrint says a woman named Meenabal first called him Periyar (1938 women's conference); other sources credit the conference itself. Spelling and attribution not cross-checked.

iyengar.mdx: sources give Iyengar as eleventh (Wikipedia mirror) or thirteenth (Encyclopedia.com) child of thirteen; existing text left unchanged. Year of Light on the Yoga Sutras of Patanjali not stated (1993 vs 1996).

pattabhi-jois.mdx: accounts conflict on the Yoga Korunta manuscript (ants: Krishnamacharya vs Jois per B. N. S. Iyengar); walk to Mysore (about 150 km, ashtangayoga.info) vs ran away with two rupees (Wikipedia). Year of marriage to Savitramma (1933) rests on ashtangayoga.info alone.
satyananda.mdx: Wikipedia says left home at 18, Hinduism Today says came to Rishikesh at 19, biharyoga.net says 20; Fellowship date 1956/1962/1963 and school 1963/1964 conflict across sources.
vinoba.mdx: father's name given as Narahar Shambhu Rao by Wikipedia only; 'death he chose' wording left as in existing text.
jyotirao-phule.mdx: Sarvajanik Satya Dharma Pustak contents could not be read this session; no new claims about it were added. Wikipedia dates the work to April 1889 and 1891.
vallalar.mdx: birth-legend details (infant laugh at Chidambaram, mirror and lamp, vision of Murugan) rest on sriramv.com and Wikipedia and are given as reported. Gazette notice of 1906 was not used.

factcheck x_expand_a: Iyengar birth order and Satyananda age on leaving home now given as ranges; Periyar title attribution now gives both ThePrint (Meenabal) and DT Next (in use from 1927). Author may want the original Hunter Commission statement for the Phule quotation.

periyar: Parents Venkatappa Nayakar and Chinnathayee Muthammal; Kannada-speaking Balija merchants; school about five years; Kashi 1904 eating-house story; Revolt 1928; Naicker dropped at Chengalpattu 1929; Malaya Dec 1929 to Jan 1930; Europe/USSR from Dec 1931, back Nov 1932; rationalism, women's rights, birth control, devadasi, script reform; 1952 registration objects -> https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Periyar

Joined Congress 1919 under Rajagopalachari; headed Madras Presidency Congress committee; jailed in non-cooperation; Unmai modelled on Pravda; arranged remarriage of widowed niece; Meenabal and the title Periyar 1938 -> https://theprint.in/theprint-profile/periyar-the-south-indian-socrates-who-smashed-brahminical-patriarchy/168020
pattabhi-jois: Father astrologer, priest, landholder; fifth of nine children; Sanskrit from age five; two rupees to Mysore 1930; Sanskrit College 1937 to 1973; series names; Williams and Gilgoff; Singleton and ashtang dand; ujjayi (Manju vs Sharath); Sharath a grandson -> https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/K._Pattabhi_Jois ; https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ashtanga_(vinyasa)_yoga

Walk of about 150 km at 15; stipend ten rupees a month March 1937; married Savitramma 1933; children 1941 to 1944; Krishnamacharya left him in charge at Mysore; B. N. S. Iyengar on manuscript; first Westerners learned three series 1975, six by 2009 -> https://www.ashtangayoga.info/philosophy/philosophy/130601-the-origins-of-ashtanga-yoga-part-13/

Mysore style: one-to-one, self-paced, memorise, first class 15 to 20 min, five or six days a week, watch half an hour first; quote 'When vinyasa is perfect, the mind is under control' -> https://archive.joisyoga.com/practice/mysore-style/
Yoga Mala: practise in order given; learn breath and vinyasa from a guru; forewords by Sharath Jois and Eddie Stern -> https://terebess.hu/english/Yoga-Mala.pdf
iyengar: Doctors predicted he would not reach 21; moved to Bangalore after father's death; failed English exam; won Krishnamacharya over by performing postures; village-to-village teaching on rice and water; Menuhin 1952 (five minutes became three hours); Belgian Queen Mother; Ramamani 1943; retired from full-time teaching 1984; props (weights, pulleys, stools, ropes); Light on Pranayama 1981, Yoga: The Path to Holistic Health 2001, Tree of Yoga 2002 -> https://www.encyclopedia.com/books/culture-magazines/iyengar-bks

Krishnamacharya sometimes withheld food; props after scooter accident; Light on Yoga in 17 languages and 3 million copies by 2005; Geeta born 1944; Iyengar practised 3 hours asana and 1 hour pranayama at 90 -> https://bafybeiemxf5abjwjbikoz4mc3a3dla6ual3jsgpdr4cjr3oz3evfyavhwq.ipfs.4everland.io/wiki/B.K.S._Iyengar.html (mirror of Wikipedia)

Quote 'focus on precision, timing, sequencing, and the use of props helps the practitioner develop awareness in any asana'; only CIYTs may call instruction Iyengar Yoga; accessible to all ages -> https://www.iynaus.org/iyengar-yoga
vinoba: Father Narahar Shambhu Rao weaver and rationalist; raised partly by grandfather Shamburao; read Gita young; brahmacharya in adolescence; 7 June 1916; Wardha 8 April 1921; Bhoodan 18 April 1951; one-sixth of land; gramdan after 1954; Brahma Vidya Mandir 1959 and its recitations; Jai Jagat -> https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Vinoba_Bhave

Brother Balkoba; 'internal uneasiness and agitation'; early 1916 burned certificates and went to Kashi; Maharashtra Dharma 1923; left Paunar 12 Sept 1951, returned 10 April 1964; target five crore acres; 23 lakh acres in Bihar 1952 to 1954; 1966, 1969, 1970 and silence year from 25 Dec 1974 -> https://www.mkgandhi.org/vinoba/bio.htm

108 sub-sections, 432 paragraphs, 540 aphorisms (Samyasutra-vritti); 24 languages; about 2.5 million copies; quote 'the Gita is meant to spiritualize human life' -> https://www.mkgandhi.org/talksongita/note.htm
satyananda: Classical education; age-six out-of-body experiences; Anandamayi Ma and Sukhman Giri; Panchagni; 1991 mandate; 1995 twelve-year Rajasooya Yajna; six branches of the Satyananda system; Fellowship 1962 Rajnandgaon -> https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Satyananda_Saraswati

Served over 12 years, edited Hindi journal; wandered about 8 years through India, Afghanistan, Nepal, Burma, Ceylon; Fellowship 1963 and school 1964; ashodashi puja ending 22 Dec 2009 -> https://www.hinduismtoday.com/hpi/2009/12/13/swami-satyananda-saraswati-attains-mahasamadhi/
1956 kriya yoga and charge to teach 'from door to door and shore to shore'; arrived Rikhia 23 Sept 1989; 1994 prediction about devotion -> https://biharyoga.net/swami-satyananda.php

Yoga Nidra: systematic rotation of consciousness from nyasa; 'yogic sleep'; birth of yoga nidra episode; sankalpa before and after, seed and watering; fixed order; heaviness then lightness; 'Do not sleep'; not necessary to concentrate; one hour like four hours' sleep -> https://www.vinyasayogaacademy.com/books/YogaNidrabySwamiSatyanandaSaraswatizliborg-200817-225446.pdf
jyotirao-phule: Father supplied flowers to Peshwa families; mother died about age one; Sagunabai; schooling interrupted and resumed through a Muslim teacher and a Christian neighbour; Board of Education 1852; Tritiya Ratna 1855 third eye; Hunter Commission 1882 proposals and quote; Ambedkar regarded him as guru -> https://epgp.inflibnet.ac.in/epgpdata/uploads/epgp_content/S000033SO/P000300/M015924/ET/146475552224ET.pdf

Marathi school 1834 to 1838; Hunter Commission statement 19 Oct 1882; widow remarriage 1860; barbers' campaign 1889; Sarvajanik Satya Dharma written 1889, released after death -> https://unipune.ac.in/chairs/mahatma_phule_chair/mphule_webfiles/life_sketch.htm
Samaj membership across castes and faiths; Deenbandhu 1877 to 1897; tamashas -> https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Satyashodhak_Samaj
Stroke 1888; Brahmananche Kasab 1869; Shivaji ballad June 1869 -> https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jyotirao_Phule
Influences: Paine, anti-slavery movements, Buddha, Kabir -> https://www.britannica.com/biography/Jyotirao-Phule
vallalar: Father died 1824; infant laugh at Chidambaram deeparadhana; lamp and mirror; Parvathi persuaded him of education; forced marriage to niece; called Vallalar; Satya Gnana Sabhai 1872 with seven screens -> https://sriramv.com/2012/05/14/arutpas-of-ramalinga-swamigal/

Vision of Murugan; 5,818 poems; Dharmasalai 1867; flag of brotherhood 22 Oct 1873 at Siddhi Valagam; doors forced open in May 1874; meat-eaters worship from outside; Kural classes -> https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ramalinga_Swamigal

Hall octagonal, 21,600-knot chain, 24 openings, five steps, three bodies, seven screens removed at 1872 dedication, locked 1873, worship at the central door with attention at root of nose, body as temple -> https://www.vallalar.org/English/VORG000000014B

First volume 1867 Asiatic Press Madras, edited by Velayuda Mudaliyar with biography; instalments 1867, 1880, 1885; modelled on Periya Purana editions; Navalar's Pooliyarutpa Maruppu; 'Calculation Ramalinga' -> https://core-prod.cambridgecore.org/core/journals/modern-asian-studies/article/print-religion-and-canon-in-colonial-india-the-publication-of-ramalinga-adigals-tiruvarutpa/8960F83457A06C714D2F938A23AC4D43
Six Thirumurai, first four published with his consent; dispute 1867 to 1904 -> https://tamil.wiki/wiki/Arutpa_Marutpa_Debate
Prayer and blessing poems paraphrased; plain language -> https://tamilnation.netlify.app/sathyam/east/vallalar/
